flaws.context: sentence 1 of 4, middle of the sentence
flaws.fix: Let your pitch move about 6.7 st across these words: lift on the stressed words and fall at the phrase end.
flaws.label: MONOTONE (recipe name)
flaws.measure: pitch range P90-P10 over the five-word window at the peak, st (reference scaled to your overall pitch range)
flaws.text: Narrower pitch range than the reference: 1.62-2.22 s ('and up the'). Your pitch range is 1.8 st here; relative to the reference rendition it is 6.7 st at your overall pitch range (1.4x the threshold; the ranges are compared as a ratio with 1 st added to each, flagged below x0.49). The span is approximate: this measure uses five-word windows. Costs 0.3 points of the reference-relative delivery index; score with this penalty removed: 95.9.
flaws.why: "if it's monotonous, your audience won't recall a word you said" (NSDA Declamation Starter Kit)

flaws.measure: mean level over the five-word window at the peak, dB re the recording's median voiced level (reference shifted by your overall level difference)
flaws.text: Lower level than the reference: 5.20-7.22 s ('House where the President and his family live.'). Relative to your own typical level you are at -13.5 dB here; the reference rendition holds -5.7 dB, 7.8 dB lower (1.8x the threshold; flagged above 4.3 dB). The span is approximate: this measure uses five-word windows. Costs 1.8 points of the reference-relative delivery index; score with this penalty removed: 97.4.
flaws.why: "Every word you deliver should come across loud and clear to the audience." (NSDA Declamation Starter Kit)

notices: Regime R1: the participant is derived from the baseline performance; 7 dimensions are enabled.

Flags are acoustic departures from reference features; pattern names describe the measured evidence, not a diagnosis. Timing is word-boundary resolution, except evidence spans: a silence or a held sound inside a word comes from 10 ms frame measures, and inserted material or a voiced run in a gap comes from the 20 ms speech-recogniser decode.
Word time is unscored: on unedited copies of the training speeches its measured word times changed too much to set a threshold, so no word-time detector is available for these edits.
Ending is unscored: in the dataset build most rising-ending edits did not raise the measured ending by 1 semitone, so too few ending edits remain to set and test a threshold.
